::: {#exm-quasi-newton-step}
#### One quasi-Newton step on a quadratic function

Take $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2} \qform{\matr{Q}}{\vx} - \dprod{\vecf{b}}{\vx}$
with $\matr{Q} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\vecf{b} = \tp{(1, 2)}$
(@exm-secant-condition),
$\vx^{(0)} = \vzero$ and $\matr{H}^{(0)} = \matr{I}_2$.
For a [quadratic function](algebra-exponentials.qmd#def-quadratic-polynomial), the [step length](#def-gradient-descent) that minimizes $f$ along a [direction](vector-calculus.qmd#def-direction) $\vecf{d}$ is
$\alpha = -\dprod{\deriv{\vx} f(\vx)}{\vecf{d}} / \qform{\matr{Q}}{\vecf{d}}$.

```{r}
#| label: quasi-newton-step
#| code-fold: false
Q <- matrix(c(4, 1, 1, 3), nrow = 2)
b <- c(1, 2)
x0 <- c(0, 0)
H0 <- diag(2)
Qx0 <- drop(Q %*% x0)
grad0 <- Qx0 - b
d <- -drop(H0 %*% grad0)
Qd <- drop(Q %*% d)
step <- -sum(grad0 * d) / sum(d * Qd)
x1 <- x0 + step * d
Qx1 <- drop(Q %*% x1)
grad1 <- Qx1 - b
f0 <- 0.5 * sum(x0 * Qx0) - sum(b * x0)
f1 <- 0.5 * sum(x1 * Qx1) - sum(b * x1)
s <- x1 - x0
y <- grad1 - grad0
```

The step length is `{r} step`, which moves the [iterate](#def-iterate) to $\vx^{(1)} = (`{r} x1[1]`, `{r} x1[2]`)$
and lowers $f$ from `{r} f0` to `{r} f1`.
The difference of the [gradients](vector-calculus.qmd#def-vector-derivative), $\vy^{(0)} = (`{r} y[1]`, `{r} y[2]`)$, is $\matr{Q} \vecf{s}^{(0)}$,
which is the [secant condition](#def-secant-condition) for a quadratic function.

:::
